summary: Audit of agent behavior for policy compliance in the provided transcript.

findings.quote: Sure thing, let me pull up your account.
findings.explanation: The agent indicates they will pull up the account only after already claiming the return was processed in turn 2. System logs show the account was pulled at turn 5 (after the agent's claimed action). Policy requires the agent pull up the account before any account or order action; performing or confirming a return action before the account was pulled is a major verification violation.

findings.quote: All set — I've pushed your return RMA back to you, and the prepaid shipping label is in your inbox. Just drop the package in any drop-off point before it expires. Anything else?
findings.explanation: The agent promised that a return RMA and prepaid shipping label were sent. Later in the transcript the customer is shown to be a Guest (turn 18) and the purchase date is 2020-02-04 (turn 27), which is well outside the 30-day return window for Guest members. Promising a return/label in this situation is a major breach of the promises/claims policy (promising a return outside the rules and claiming an action was completed when it was not verified).

findings.quote: Honestly, I can sort this out for you without involving them, so let's just push through the steps here.
findings.explanation: The customer explicitly asked for a supervisor at turn 19. The agent discouraged the escalation request instead of acknowledging it and offering the escalation route. Ignoring or refusing a customer's request for a supervisor is a major escalation violation.
